correctness.rationale: For a three-person SIR chain starting (2,1,0), the exact triangular forward equations for A,B,D yield the displayed explicit probabilities. The at-risk pair masses W1=2A+D and W2=2B imply the covariance identity. The h ratio has uniformly positive lambda derivative at sufficiently small t and uniformly negative log derivative at sufficiently large t on any fixed [a,b] with a>0. Covariance strictness follows from the independent-copy integral under the nondegenerate positive measure Q_t. Continuity gives a crossing. Standalone seven-state uniformization agreed with every closed form in 126 comparisons; 217 assertions passed. Computational checks are corroboration rather than infinite-distribution proof.

value.rationale: The smallest closed population permitting one and two infectious persons alongside susceptibles admits a universal sign reversal of inferred per-pair transmissibility for every nondegenerate bounded positive heterogeneity law. Unlike a routine numerical example, the theorem establishes a structural observation-window effect, showing that fixed microscopically linear hazards can appear increasingly then decreasingly dependent on concurrent infectious count. It clarifies why late-time depletion/recovery confounds naive nonlinear contagion inference; late at-risk data are rare and no empirical power guarantee is claimed.
